method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a dates module (rtw-dates.l4, built-in date functions only), a seat-neutral core (rtw-core.l4, with 14 regulative rules for the duties and powers of the worker, the employer and the Corporation) and two seat layers (rtw-seat.l4 for the injured worker and, on a death, the family; rtw-seat-employer.l4 for the employer) that restate no rule; no REFUSE (a case the text does not answer returns an explicit not-covered value, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate. Corrected on 2026-10-24 after an independent verification: one wrong expected value (s 30(5), a claim received on a public holiday, finding 19), rule content moved from the seats into the core, regulative rules added for s 18(4a), s 48(6)-(7) and s 100(1), s 59(6) encoded, every NOT parenthesised, findings 10 and 18 corrected.
edition_encoded: Return to Work Act 2014 (SA), Open Australian Legal Corpus text as at 2024-12-01 (version_id south_australian_legislation:2024-12-01/2014.16.un, scraped 2025-03-10), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/return-to-work-act-2014.txt; with the Return to Work Regulations 2015 (SA), corpus text as at 2024-12-01 (version_id south_australian_legislation:2024-12-01/2015.29.un, scraped 2025-03-10), as deposited at ../../../return-to-work-regulations-2015/registers/source-bundle/return-to-work-regulations-2015.txt. Not the official text; may be out of date; every indexed amount after 2024-12-01 is an input.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run rtw-dates.l4 ; l4 run rtw-core.l4 ; l4 run rtw-seat.l4 ; l4 run rtw-seat-employer.l4 ; l4 run rtw-cases-core.l4 ; l4 run rtw-cases-worker.l4 ; l4 run rtw-cases-employer.l4
checks.result: 443 assertions satisfied (215 core, 161 worker seat, 67 employer seat including 33 mirror cases), 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24, after the corrections); 13 #TRACEs with an expect line (7 breaches, 6 obligations still open), each read and as expected
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: Coverage: s 4(1) (worker, employer, contract of service, business day, notional weekly earnings), s 4(2), (4), (9), (17), regs 5, 6, 8; s 7(1), (2), (4), (7)-(10). Notice and claim: s 16(1)-(4), (6) with reg 11; s 30(1)-(6), (10) with reg 19; s 31(4); s 32(2). Weekly payments: s 5 with regs 7, 9 (the s 5(12)(b) overtime component an input, its formula missing); ss 36-39; s 40 with reg 26; s 41; s 42 with reg 27; s 43; s 44; s 48(1)-(10), (12) with reg 28. Seriously injured workers: s 21(2), (3), (5), (8), with the s 22 assessment an input. Suitable work and termination: s 18(1)-(4e) (including s 18(4a)), (6), (7) with reg 12; s 20. Medical expenses and property: s 33(20), (21) with reg 23; s 35 with reg 25. Lump sums: ss 55, 56 with Schedules 6, 7 (the s 56(4) formula is missing, so not covered, with the s 56(11) ceiling); ss 57, 58 with reg 34, Schedule 8 and Regulations Schedule 1. Death: s 59(1)(a)-(c) at total dependency, (5), (6), (7); s 61 with reg 35(2); s 62 with reg 35(3). Common law and review: s 72(1), (3); s 99(2); s 100. Regs reg 4 indexation, indexed amounts as inputs. Out: Part 3 service standards in detail, s 59(1) partial dependency and (1)(d) other relatives, s 59(2)-(4), (8)-(16), redemptions (ss 53-54), s 56A, ss 8-12, 34, 45-47, 49-52, 60, 63-69, the s 33(1)-(2) scales, Part 5 beyond s 72, Tribunal procedure, Parts 7 onward (registration, premiums including the s 142 formula, self-insurance, the Corporation). Read with subjects/au/social-security-act-1991/encodings/baseline-2026-10/ (age pension age for s 44; Part 3.14 compensation, unverified), subjects/au/income-tax-assessment-act-1997/ (unverified) and subjects/au/sa/victims-of-crime-act-2001/ (s 17(5)(b) takes this encoding's s 58 and death answers as an input); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the injured worker (and, on a death, the worker's partner, children and the person who pays for the funeral)
the employer (the pre-injury employer in s 18); a self-insured employer is outside ss 16(6), 30(5), 30(6)
